Any financial matter referred by the President

blocks.content: The Finance Commission is constituted by the President under Article 280 of the Constitution mainly to give its recommendations on distribution of tax revenues between the Union and the States.

rows: Share of net tax proceeds transferred from the Union to all States
Allocation of the total state share among individual States
Correcting fiscal imbalance between Centre and States
Ensuring equity and correcting regional disparities among States
Constitutional assignment of revenues vs. functional responsibilities
Criteria like Income Distance, Population, Forest Cover, and Fiscal Effort

items: Recommendations of the Finance Commission are purely advisory and not binding on the Union Government.
Qualifications for members are specified by Parliament via the Finance Commission (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1951, rather than directly in Article 280.
Members of the Finance Commission are eligible for reappointment.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Article 280 of the Constitution establishes the Finance Commission as a quasi-judicial advisory body.
The Commission is constituted by the President of India every five years or at an earlier time as deemed necessary.
It recommends the allocation of the net proceeds of divisible taxes between the Union and the States.
It formulates principles governing Grants-in-Aid to States under Article 275 out of the Consolidated Fund of India.
It evaluates measures to augment the State Consolidated Fund to supplement the resources of Panchayats and Municipalities.
